name: Pan-Turkism
summary: Pan-Turkism seeks the cultural and, for its stronger strands, political unity of the Turkic peoples across the borders that divide them, from the Balkans and Anatolia through the Caucasus and Central Asia to Siberia and Xinjiang. It arose among Russian-Turkic and late-Ottoman intellectuals who judged Ottomanism and pan-Islamism unworkable and placed the nation, defined by language and culture or by race, above religion. Its strands differ sharply on race, on borders and on how far the union is political, so many positions are splits.
scope: The national question only: Gasprinski's unity of language, mind and action, Akçura's 1904 'Three Types of Policy', Gökalp's Turkism and its programme, the racist-Turanist strand of Atsız, and the state-level Organization of Turkic States as a heir that respects existing borders. It excludes the programmes of the parties and governments that carry the idea (economy, welfare, foreign policy beyond the national question), Türkeş's Nine Lights nationalism (which defines itself as Turkey-bound 'Turkishness' and is used only to show where strands differ), Kemalist Anatolia-only nationalism and pseudo-Turkology.

keyFigures.name: Yusuf Akçura
keyFigures.role: Author of 'Three Types of Policy' (1904), the first manifesto of political Turkism.

keyFigures.name: Ziya Gökalp
keyFigures.role: Main ideologue of Turkism, who defined the nation by culture and framed the Turkist programme.

keyFigures.name: Ismail Gasprinski
keyFigures.role: Crimean Tatar reformer who preached unity of language, mind and action among Turks.

sources.title: Three types of policy (Üç tarz-ı siyaset), Yusuf Akçura, 1904, translated excerpts with editorial introduction

sources.author: Nihal Atsız

sources.title: Pan-Turkism and Islam in Russia (Harvard University Press, 1967; archive.org partial copy)
sources.author: Serge A. Zenkovsky
sources.usedFor: Gasprinski's unity of language, mind and action and his acceptance of Russia, Akçura's Turkic union, the 1905 Moslem congress, cultural versus territorial autonomy among Russian Turks.

Positions held by one thinker only (women's equality, democracy, state economy, leader and party rule) are null.
